limitations: Uniform hidden worlds, assumed branch opening, no observed opponent history, bot continuations, first eligible per deal, two changed ends, exploratory CIs, no block winner. Selected equal-pip two-action positions are not representative of all moves; pass probability is computed from uniformly allocated hidden worlds and first opponent response; first eligible per deal, possible correlated seeds; intervals exploratory; pass-gap stratification is post-action; no train/test oracle evaluation.
next: Fresh independent holdout; incorporate observed opponent history into hidden-world posterior.
checkpoint: Independent 60-position exact hidden-world holdout; high next-opponent pass chance vs paired win chance
passVsWinMethod: For each row with nonzero passDelta, higher-pass win advantage = sign(passDelta) * policy.win (connector minus unrelated). Regret relative to best of two on same hidden worlds = max(0,-advantage). This oracle is IN-SAMPLE and NOT a deployable policy. Strata use next opponent hand size and absolute pass probability difference.
newFinding: In this independent 60-position set, choosing the move with greater chance of making the next opponent pass has +0.3356 mean within-position finish-first advantage over the other equal-pip move across 45 non-tied pass forecasts under closed-branch-control; only +0.0385 under fast-doubles. No claim of human-game causal effect.
confidence: Model-specific repeat signal for closed-branch-control and min-hand-pips; 45 informative positions, 577 exact hidden allocations across 60 positions; opponent one-stone stratum n=3 too small.
exactNextAction: Implement train/test split of exact hidden worlds per position, select win-maximizing move on train worlds, compare out-of-sample against higher-pass choice on test worlds using matched continuation seeds; increase worlds for thin positions and report decision regret and minus risk.
